messages:
anya: Heads up — saw a small perf regression on prod GPU pool this morning. p99 latency jumped ~120ms for a short window on g4s-prod-3. Correlates with heavy KV cache churn during continuous-batching bursts. Posting quick traces and a couple hypotheses.

anya: top of flamegraph around step_run -> attention_kernels::fused_gemm on the large sequence path, and frequent KV eviction spikes (~40MB/s transient). Snippet from perf dump: 
```
2026-03-18T09:12:03Z GPU0 free_mem: 1.1GB used_mem: 14.9GB
batch formation tokens: 918 avg_kv_hits: 0.63 kv_evicted_bytes: 42MB/s
kernel chosen: fused_gemm_fp16_fast
ooms: 0 (soft throttle triggered)
```

brett: Thanks. Do you have the kernel selection log (why fused_gemm was picked) and the batching admission events around the spike? Might be kernel selection + batch size alignment making transient footprint > headroom.

anya: attaching a snippet from admission log: 
```
[09:11:58] admit request id=R7821 tokens=645 kv_resident=0.52 budget_target=1024 chosen_batch_tokens=900
[09:11:58] admit request id=R7822 tokens=220 kv_resident=0.15 budget_target=1024 chosen_batch_tokens=300
[09:11:59] batch formed total_tokens=1220 kv_total_resident=0.47 -> triggered kernel fused_gemm_fp16_fast
```

perf-bot: Metric alert - gpu_mem_headroom < 1.2GB for pool g4s-prod-3 between 09:11:50-09:12:10, bursty kv-evict-rate > 35MB/s

liam: My take: two interacting things — (1) continuous batcher allowed a large aggregate token batch that, together with KV cache misalignment, pushed ephemeral memory past headroom; (2) kernel selection chose a higher-throughput kernel with larger workspace. We should gate batch formation by a KV-footprint-aware token budget, not a single global token target.

marie: Agreed. Also want to explore kernel fallback: if chosen kernel's workspace_estimate + kv_estimate > headroom -> pick lower-workspace kernel (even if slightly slower). We have telemetry for kernel_workspace_estimate per model variant.

brett: Can we simulate this quickly? Two experiments: A) dynamic token_budget = base * (1 - kv_miss_factor) B) kernel_fallback_enabled where we prefer int8_gemm when workspace estimate > threshold. Run on canary nodes 3 and 4 for 2 hours.

anya: I ran a quick staging run overnight. Reducing max_batch_tokens from 1024 -> 600 (static) eliminated the OOM-like headroom dips, p99 improved a bit but overall throughput dropped ~7%. Kernel fallback reduced mem spikes but increased median latency ~30ms.

liam: Ok so tradeoff surface is expected. We might do a hybrid: keep base budget but enforce per-request token caps when kv_resident < 0.4, and enable soft kernel fallback only when headroom < 1.5GB. That should preserve throughput for healthy-cache loads.

brett: Nice. Let's define measurable success criteria: no headroom < 1GB events for the canary window, throughput drop < 5% and p95 latency change within +/- 20ms. If pass, roll to pool. If fail, revert.

anya: Proposed experiment steps:
1) deploy dynamic token budget logic to canary nodes (flag: kv_budget_gate=true)
2) enable kernel_fallback soft (flag: kernel_fallback=soft) with workspace threshold = 1.6GB
3) instrument metrics: kv_eviction_rate, kernel_workspace_chosen, batch_total_tokens, gpu_mem_headroom, request_throughput
4) run for 2 hours during peak window (tomorrow 09:00-11:00 UTC)

perf-bot: Quick summary from last staging run -> {"max_headroom_drop": 0.9GB, "avg_throughput": 188 req/s, "p99_delta": +120ms} (posted by perf-bot at 09:05)

sre-oncall: Heads-up — if this touches admission logic, make sure to add circuit-breaker to avoid any regression cascade. We should also set an automated rollback if headroom < 800MB for > 30s.

liam: I'll run the sim harness across the model suite today and upload a perf profile. Expect artifacts in s3://redwood-perf/sim/kvcache/2263456789/ by EOD.

anya: Assigning: liam -> sim harness + kernel_workspace telemetry, marie -> kernel fallback impl + perf regression test, brett -> rollout plan and canary orchestration, anya -> collect and publish probe dashboards + compare historical headroom baselines.

brett: Cool. If anyone spots an easier immediate mitigation, we can flip a config to reduce default max_batch_tokens on the pool until experiments complete.

marie: small note — kernel selection logs currently approximate workspace; I'll add a quick microbenchmark to tighten estimates (adds ~1% overhead to model init).

anya: Thanks all. Will post a short follow-up thread with exact feature flags and rollout YAML. :white_check_mark:

liam: +1, will ping when sim artifacts are up.

perf-bot: Canary test scheduled for 2026-03-19T09:00:00Z with flags {kv_budget_gate:true,kernel_fallback:soft}. Monitoring channels: #eng-runtime, #incidents.

brett: Great work coordinating. Let's keep the canary tight and revert fast if we see headroom regressions.

anya: ending notes — primary hypothesis: KV cache misalignment increases transient memory while continuous batching aggregates large token counts -> push over workspace for high-throughput kernels. Experiment aims to tune admission heuristics and kernel selection to avoid OOM without regressing throughput too much.
